_comment: ProgHUB judge-runner seccomp profile. Strategy: allow-by-default, deny a curated list of syscalls that are never required by sandboxed Python/Node user code and which materially increase kernel attack surface or container-escape risk. This is INTENTIONALLY more permissive than a strict whitelist profile, because the judge-runner must reliably execute arbitrary (Python/Node) student code; a too-strict whitelist tends to break new language runtime versions silently. Dangerous syscalls are explicitly blocked with EPERM (errno 1). Operators MUST read docs/operations/sandbox.md before enabling this in production and SHOULD follow up with a stricter whitelist profile once the supported runtime matrix is stable.

syscalls.comment: Denylist: filesystem mounts, kernel module loading, ptrace/VM cross-inspection, namespace manipulation, time/host manipulation, swap, quotas, perf, BPF, kexec. None are required by standard Python/Node program execution.

args.comment: CLONE_NEWUSER = 0x10000000. Deny only user-namespace clone calls; ordinary clone/fork is required for subprocess-based Python/Node execution.

syscalls.comment: clone3 passes flags through a pointer that seccomp cannot inspect, so deny it with ENOSYS to avoid CLONE_NEWUSER bypass while allowing runtimes to fall back to clone.
